raw_case_text: A 52-year-old female born in Guatemala presented with complaints of diffuse headache, right-sided neck pain, vomiting and photophobia which started 3 days prior to presentation. She denied any recent travel or illness but confirmed that her spouse had multiple incarcerations. On presentation she was found afebrile and hemodynamically stable. She complained of paravertebral and upper thoracic spine discomfort with negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs on examination. Initial CBC showed no evidence of anemia or leukocytosis. Initial CT of the head showed no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, mass-effect, hydrocephalus or midline shift. CT of the chest showed numerous submillimeter sized bilateral lung nodules, with scattered calcifications (Fig. 1). The chemistry panel was within normal range. The lumbar puncture performed on admission revealed colorless clear fluid with a white blood cell count 278/mm3, red blood cell count 35/mm3, glucose 26 mg/dL (ref 40-70 mg/dL) and protein 147 mg/dL (ref 15-45 mg/dL). Manual differentiation of the CSF revealed lymphocytes 48%, neutrophils 47% and mononuclear cells 3%. An MRI of the brain with contrast demonstrated greater than 40 submillimeter, similar in size to the lesions seen in the lungs, enhancing foci in the supratentorial brain, infratentorial brain and brainstem along with dural enhancement suggestive of a meningoencephalitis (Fig. 2). The patient was initially started on vancomycin, ceftriaxone, ampicillin and acyclovir although these were discontinued as PCR for typical viral and bacterial meningeal infectious etiologies was negative. IGRA of the serum was negative revealing Nil .03 IU/mL, Mitogen-Nil 9.50 IU/mL, TB1-Nil .01 IU/mL and TB2-Nil .01 IU/mL. Sputum Acid Fast Bacillus (AFB) stain and culture and CSF AFB stain and culture were also obtained and were all initially negative. CSF fungal cultures resulted negative. A sample of the initial CSF was sent to pathology for further review. Unfortunately, adenosine deaminase (ADA) was not recorded from the initial sample. During her hospital stay, she continued to experience progressive encephalopathy and agitation eventually requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. Repeat CT of the head on hospital day 5 revealed dilated lateral and 3rd ventricles requiring extra ventricular drain placement by neurosurgery. Given high clinical suspicion for tb, despite negative testing to date, she was started on rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol (RIPE) and methylprednisolone 40 mg every 8 h in addition to vancomycin and cefepime. The next day, pathology from the initial CSF sample revealed findings suggestive of granulomatous inflammation potentially consistent with TB. On hospital day 19 initial CSF AFB culture returned positive and was sent for confirmatory testing which revealed Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. Unfortunately despite initiation of RIPE therapy and corticosteroids, she continued to exhibit significant neurologic decline. She eventually required tracheostomy and percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy tube placement and is evidencing an overall poor prognosis.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 52-year-old Guatemalan-born female presented with a 3-day history of diffuse headache, right-sided neck pain, vomiting, and photophobia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Three days prior to presentation, the patient developed acute diffuse headache, right-sided neck pain, upper thoracic/paravertebral discomfort, vomiting, and photophobia.
subjective.past_medical_history: Born in Guatemala; denied recent travel or prior illness, though her spouse had a history of multiple incarcerations.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for headache, neck and upper thoracic back pain, vomiting, and photophobia.

objective.physical_examination: Afebrile and hemodynamically stable on presentation; paravertebral and upper thoracic spine discomfort with negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs. Subsequently developed progressive encephalopathy and agitation requiring endotracheal intubation.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial CBC and serum chemistry panel were normal. Serum IGRA (QuantiFERON) was negative (Nil 0.03 IU/mL, Mitogen-Nil 9.50 IU/mL, TB1-Nil 0.01 IU/mL, TB2-Nil 0.01 IU/mL). Sputum AFB stain and culture were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial non-contrast head CT was normal; repeat head CT on hospital day 5 showed hydrocephalus with dilated lateral and third ventricles. Chest CT showed numerous submillimeter bilateral miliary lung nodules with scattered calcifications. Contrast-enhanced brain MRI demonstrated >40 submillimeter enhancing parenchymal foci throughout the supratentorial brain, infratentorial brain, and brainstem with dural enhancement. Admission lumbar puncture yielded clear colorless CSF with WBC 278/mm^3 (48% lymphocytes, 47% neutrophils, 3% mononuclear cells), RBC 35/mm^3, glucose 26 mg/dL (reference: 40–70 mg/dL), and protein 147 mg/dL (reference: 15–45 mg/dL); multiplex viral/bacterial PCR, fungal culture, and initial CSF AFB smear were negative, while CSF cytology/pathology showed granulomatous inflammation.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Initial CSF AFB culture returned positive on hospital day 19 and was confirmed as Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, establishing the diagnosis of miliary tuberculosis with tuberculous meningoencephalitis and hydrocephalus. The patient underwent external ventricular drain placement on day 5 and was started on empirical RIPE therapy (rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol) and intravenous methylprednisolone 40 mg every 8 hours, but she experienced persistent neurological decline requiring tracheostomy and PEG tube placement with a poor prognosis.
